problems.title: Theorem 1 bound is independent of head classification accuracy
problems.evidence: r_ij=min(eta_i_star,eta_j) makes both pairwise minima equal; independent_check_output.json
problems.assumptions: All stated ratios, including ties and natural budget orderings
problems.counterevidence: The inequality may still be true and the full confusion-weighted expression may vary
problems.impact: Invalidates the claimed dependency of the theoretical lower bound, not empirical gains
problems.repair: Derive a sharper conditional bound or withdraw the dependence claim
problems.repair_verification: Cancellation proven algebraically; no replacement theorem verified

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Physically viewed and read p.5 Theorem 1, Eq.(7), Remark 1. For any permitted ratios (including equality) the defined r_ij equals min(eta_i_star,eta_j). The classification probabilities and lambda do not alter this algebra.
independent_check.decisive_check: min(r11,r22)=min(eta1_star,eta1,eta2_star,eta2)=min(r21,r12), so the coefficient of Phead is exactly zero. The example (0.02,0.8,0.01,1) yields both minima 0.01; lower bound=0.01 lambda for every Phead. Ordered budgets and ties cannot remove equality.
independent_check.counterevidence: The weighted pre-minimum expression may vary with class-specific confusion probabilities and the resulting loose inequality can be true. Remark 1 explicitly identifies the lower bound as the worst-case accuracy at issue; thus these alternatives do not rescue its claimed Phead sensitivity.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major retained: the central head-identification-to-retention theoretical justification is invalid, regardless of surviving empirical speedups. Narrow the interpretation to a constant bound or prove a sharper class-conditional bound; no new theorem established.

problems.title: Risk concentration is not a bound on classification accuracy as stated
problems.location: p.5 Lemma 1, Eq.(6) and transition to Theorem 1
problems.evidence: Probability scopes differ; BCE range/tail and prediction/sampling assumptions missing; generic rare-loss calculation
problems.assumptions: Counterexample addresses generic unrestricted BCE justification, not measured CV data
problems.counterevidence: Moving confidence term inside parentheses can fix typography, but does not establish missing bridge
problems.impact: The proposed theoretical guarantee remains unsupported
problems.repair: Specify loss/sampling model, valid concentration and classification conversion

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: The p.5 image confirms log(2/delta) and that the confidence addend lies outside probability parentheses. Read the lemma definition of BCE-induced F and following assignment P1+P2=Phead; source search finds no separate proof or defined conversion elsewhere.
independent_check.decisive_check: Even if parentheses are corrected, a singleton loss from constant predicted probability exp(-100), iid Bernoulli(0.01) labels has mean about 1. At N=100 the no-positive-label event has probability 0.99^100 about 0.366, empirical loss about 0 and signed singleton conditional Rademacher mean zero. A range-free sqrt(log(40)/100) about 0.192 correction cannot cover this with probability 0.95. More decisively, a probability of a reference-sample uniform-risk event is not new-head accuracy, and setting its complement equal to head misclassification events is not a valid decomposition without an explicit label/sampling/calibration model.
independent_check.counterevidence: The generic BCE example is not established as a realizable CV head/data configuration; the report properly calls it a challenge to an unrestricted justification, not an observed CateKV counterexample. A restricted bounded CV-derived class could avoid it but needs definition. Moving parentheses alone does not fix the distinct event mismatch.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major for the demonstrated unsupported core derivation/bridge, not proof that every possible repaired bound is false. A valid concentration theorem needs a specified sampling/loss class and a separate classification conversion; that replacement remains Needs Evidence.

problems.title: Multi-alpha static classification accumulates masks from earlier ratios
problems.evidence: List initialization before alpha loop; explicit three-sample finite example
problems.assumptions: At least two alpha values in one function call as in main block
problems.counterevidence: Single-alpha calls unaffected; experimental generation path unknown
problems.impact: Order-dependent release masks; historical results Needs Evidence
problems.repair: Initialize selected_matrices inside alpha loop; define tie policy
problems.repair_verification: Independent per-alpha calculation differs; author code not executed

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Static select_headmask/static.py:41-83 and main multi-alpha list :90-98 were read. At least two alpha values are required; three sampled files is a valid files_per_subfolder parameter for the finite example.
independent_check.decisive_check: For score rows (0,1,2,3),(0,2,1,3),(3,0,1,2), alpha=.25 selects each unique minimum, counts (2,1,0,0). Alpha=.5 selects lowest two, isolated counts (2,2,2,0), while the list surviving the first alpha yields (4,3,2,0). The top-ceil(.5*4) count threshold is 2 in the isolated case, giving mask (1,1,1,0), versus 3 accumulated, giving (1,1,0,0). This demonstrates invocation-order dependence, with no code import.
independent_check.counterevidence: Single-alpha calls are unaffected; ties can independently select more than the nominal fraction. The pinned release and example main call do not identify historical mask-generation invocations.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor later-release bug with published effect Needs Evidence. Move selected_matrices=[] inside each alpha loop; treat exact-count tie handling separately. Only the index/count arithmetic is verified, not a corrected production run.
